hints.title: Draw who finished ahead
hints.body: Write the five initials. Draw an arrow from each faster runner to each slower runner named in the question. Follow chains of arrows too.
hints.recap: A chain of comparisons can fix a finishing position.
hints.pitfall: Only use comparisons stated or forced by the question.
hints.pause: Look for a runner who must be ahead of, or behind, everyone else.

recall.reminder: A chain of comparisons can fix a finishing position.

hints.title: Count the remaining orders
hints.body: Once any fixed positions are filled, count the orders of the remaining runners. Check the restriction involving Hermione and Lavender: swapping those two reverses their order.
hints.recap: Pairing arrangements can show how many satisfy an order restriction.
hints.pitfall: Do not count both orders when the question permits only one.
hints.pause: Check that the swap preserves the other restrictions, then count valid finishes.

recall.reminder: List the possible orders systematically, keeping only those that satisfy every comparison.

solution:
George must be last because each other runner is known to finish before him, directly or through Hermione preceding Lavender.

Of the 4!=24 orders of the other runners, exactly half have Hermione before Lavender: swapping their names pairs a valid order with an invalid one. The number is 24/2=12. Answer C.
knowledgePattern: Count linear orders under a partial order
